item.definition: A 6-sided polygon with six equal sides, six interior angles of 120°, composed of six equilateral triangles around its center.

item.description: Any point situated on the perpendicular bisector of a line segment XY is equidistant from endpoints X and Y.

item.property_name: Central Angle Property of Regular Hexagon
item.statement: Six 60° equilateral triangle central angles meet at the center of a regular hexagon, totaling 360°.

item.rule_text: The compass radius must be set strictly greater than half the length of the line segment (> 0.5 XY) for arcs to intersect.

steps: 1. Given line segment XY, open compass with radius > 0.5 XY.
2. With center X, draw arcs above and below segment XY.
3. With center Y and same radius, draw arcs intersecting previous arcs at A and B.
4. Join line AB. Line AB bisects segment XY at a 90° angle.
1. Draw a ray with vertex A.
2. With center A, draw a arc intersecting the ray at point B.
3. With center B and identical compass radius, draw an arc intersecting first arc at C.
1. Draw a circle of radius r with center O.
3. Using same radius r, step off consecutive points B, C, D, E, F around circumference.
4. Connect line segments AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA to complete regular hexagon.

item.relationship_name: Equilateral Triangle Angle and Hexagon Central Angle
item.description: The interior angle of an equilateral triangle (60°) equals the central angle of a regular hexagon, six of which complete a 360° circle.
